headline: Searchlight Capital faces a 60-day Splunk renewal lock-in window and a June DORA audit, creating an immediate window to displace Splunk with Elastic as a unified SIEM and observability platform that cuts storage costs by 40% and delivers DORA dashboards natively.

sections.heading: Strategic Context
bullets: Splunk renewal locks in 60 days (March 15, 2027), triggering a $1.2M annual commitment with auto-renewal; Priya Sharma (VP Platform) and Sandra Park (CFO) control the go/no-go decision and own commercial sign-off.

DORA audit in June 2026 requires operational resilience dashboards (deployment frequency, MTTR, change failure rate, lead time) across portfolio infrastructure; James Liu (Lead SRE) must deliver these for compliance attestation.

Current Splunk bill is $1.2M annually with $340K/year locked in storage tier costs for 7-year audit retention; Elastic frozen tier with searchable snapshots on S3 cuts retention costs by 40% without performance degradation.
Searchlight Capital just closed $4.2B Fund V (announced May 4), crossing $14B AUM; operational excellence and audit readiness are now portfolio-wide expectations.

sections.heading: Recent Signals
bullets: Fund V close (May 4) signals increased due-diligence rigor on portfolio operations; DORA compliance is now a governance requirement, not a nicety.
DORA analyst note (April 19) cites Searchlight Capital explicitly, confirming June audit is real and high-stakes for asset manager credibility.
Priya and James signaled in prior meeting that POC must prove 2.4 TB/day ingest with p99 query latency under 200 ms; no wiggle room on performance benchmarks.

sections.heading: Likely Pain Points
bullets: Storage tier costs at 7-year retention are driving architecture council cost reviews; Splunk warm and cold tier administration consumes 15-20% of James Liu's team bandwidth with no native remediation tooling.
DORA dashboard delivery timeline is tight (8 weeks to June audit); Splunk's out-of-the-box DORA support is minimal, requiring custom development or a third-party app.
Splunk AutoOps equivalent does not exist; each cluster health check currently requires a $15K-25K Professional Services engagement, delaying troubleshooting and audit prep.
Frozen tier query latency against the 18-month compliance window (audit pull) is a known friction point; Searchlight Capital's audit team has complained about multi-minute query times on cold data.

sections.heading: Discovery Questions
bullets: James: can you walk us through how many DORA compliance queries run monthly during audit prep, and which ones today time out or require manual SLA exceptions?
Priya: if we cut Splunk storage costs by 40% while improving compliance query performance, what would you reinvest in (headcount, other observability gaps, or a line-item reduction)?
Sandra: are there any contractual penalties if we exit Splunk before the March 2027 renewal, or is this a clean 60-day window to avoid lock-in?
James: how many of your current 14 Splunk indexes are read-heavy for compliance vs. operational SIEMs? Can we segment the migration in two waves to reduce risk?

sections.heading: Talking Points
bullets: Single platform advantage: Elastic replaces Splunk SIEM + Datadog APM with one unified observability stack, eliminating Datadog APM seat licenses (~$150K/year estimated), reducing tool sprawl, and streamlining SOC workflows.

DORA ready out of the box: Elastic Observability includes native DORA dashboards (deployment frequency, MTTR, change failure rate, lead time) integrated with GitLab CI; Splunk has no equivalent, requiring 4-6 weeks of custom development or a $10K app license.

AutoOps (free for all Elastic tiers) monitors 100+ cluster and index health metrics continuously, surfaces root-cause diagnostics, and provides ready-to-run remediation commands. This replaces Splunk's PS-driven cluster health checks ($15K-25K per engagement); total cost avoidance is $30K-50K/year.

Frozen tier with searchable snapshots: 18-month compliance queries return in 2-5 seconds (not 60+ seconds in Splunk); 7-year retention on S3 at $150K/year (vs. Splunk's $340K/year), freeing $190K annually and improving audit team productivity.

sections.heading: Risks and Open Questions
bullets: POC must prove 2.4 TB/day ingest at p99 under 200 ms query latency across 14 indexes; if benchmark fails, James will default back to Splunk renewal. Schedule load-test with production-like shard topology and query patterns by May 18.

Sandra Park has not yet validated budget headroom for migration costs (Elastic licenses, data transfer, professional services for architecture and DORA dashboard customization); need a commercial review call with CFO by May 21 to avoid scope creep.
Splunk contract language may include early exit penalties or commit true-ups; legal review of the termination terms must happen before the 30-day go/no-go decision (due June 10).

Datadog APM integration risk: if James's team has built custom workflows on Datadog APM, the migration to Elastic APM may require re-testing; confirm whether Datadog is a hard blocker or a nice-to-have in the discovery call.
